source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 9–17 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 256 original source records are bound exactly once.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Names the hearing kings and retains six peoples and all three geographical zones.
verses.before: When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan in the hill country, in the foothills, and along all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—heard of it,
verses.after: The kings west of the Jordan heard what had happened—the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, the lowlands, and along the whole coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan in the hill country, in the foothills, and along all the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—heard of it,

verses.rationale: Unfolds one mouth as united purpose while keeping the two named opponents.
verses.before: they gathered together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel.
verses.after: They joined forces with one purpose: to fight Joshua and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: they gathered together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel.

verses.rationale: Uses the contrast to introduce a different response without adding a motive before their later explanation.
verses.before: But the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
verses.after: But the people of Gibeon, hearing what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
verses.tsw_comparator: But the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,

verses.rationale: Renders the difficult envoy verb without adopting a provision-reading silently; retains the deceptive equipment.
verses.before: and they acted craftily. They went and prepared provisions and took worn-out sacks on their donkeys and worn-out wineskins, torn and patched,
verses.after: devised a cunning plan of their own. They set out posing as envoys, with worn-out sacks on their donkeys and old wineskins that were split and tied up.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they acted craftily. They went and prepared provisions and took worn-out sacks on their donkeys and worn-out wineskins, torn and patched,

verses.rationale: Keeps the staged wear and dry bread, with a note on crumbling versus moldy.
verses.before: worn-out and patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out clothes on themselves. All the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbled.
verses.after: They wore patched, worn-out sandals and old clothes. All the bread they took for provisions was dry and crumbling.
verses.tsw_comparator: worn-out and patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out clothes on themselves. All the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbled.

verses.rationale: Identifies the audience and preserves covenant as the requested relationship.
verses.before: They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now therefore make a covenant with us.”
verses.after: They came to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and told him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now therefore make a covenant with us.”

verses.rationale: Makes the collective singulars natural while preserving the suspicion and Hivite identification.
verses.before: The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you live among us. How then can we make a covenant with you?”
verses.after: The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you live among us. How could we make a covenant with you then?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you live among us. How then can we make a covenant with you?”

verses.rationale: Retains the evasive service claim before Joshua’s direct questions.
verses.before: They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Who are you, and where do you come from?”
verses.after: “We are your servants,” they told Joshua. “Who are you, and where do you come from?” Joshua asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Who are you, and where do you come from?”

verses.rationale: Preserves their claimed distant origin and appeal to the divine name and fame.
verses.before: They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard the report of him and all that he did in Egypt,
verses.after: They answered, “Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of the LORD your God. We have heard of his fame and everything he did in Egypt,
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard the report of him and all that he did in Egypt,

verses.rationale: Keeps both kings, their territories, and Og’s specific location without adding the nearer victories they omit.
verses.before: and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
verses.after: and everything he did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who was in Ashtaroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

verses.rationale: Reduces a third speech level by indirect reporting inside the quoted elders’ instruction, preserving every request.
verses.before: Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, ‘Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them and say to them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’
verses.after: Our elders and everyone in our land told us, ‘Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them. Tell them you are their servants and ask them to make a covenant with you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, ‘Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them and say to them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’

verses.rationale: Retains the false warm-to-dry evidence and the invitation to inspect it.
verses.before: This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses as food on the day we went out to come to you. But now look, it is dry and crumbled.
verses.after: This bread was still warm when we took it from our homes on the day we set out to meet you. Look at it now—dry and crumbling!
verses.tsw_comparator: This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses as food on the day we went out to come to you. But now look, it is dry and crumbled.

verses.rationale: Keeps each piece of staged evidence and the emphatic length claim.
verses.before: These wineskins were new when we filled them, and look, they are torn. And these clothes and sandals of ours are worn out because of the very long journey.”
verses.after: These wineskins were new when we filled them, but now they are split. And these clothes and sandals have worn out on the very long journey.”
verses.tsw_comparator: These wineskins were new when we filled them, and look, they are torn. And these clothes and sandals of ours are worn out because of the very long journey.”

verses.rationale: Retains took without deciding whether they tasted, inspected, or shared the food; counsel renders asking the LORD’s mouth.
verses.before: So the men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask the mouth of the LORD.
verses.after: The men of Israel took some of their provisions, but they did not ask for the LORD’s counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask the mouth of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes peace, covenant, life protection and the leaders’ sworn commitment.
verses.before: Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore to them.
verses.after: Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant to let them live. The leaders of the assembly swore an oath to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the elapsed three days and the discovery’s direct contradiction of the claim.
verses.before: At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors and were living among them.
verses.after: Three days after making the covenant, the Israelites learned that these people were their neighbors and lived among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, they heard that they were their neighbors and were living among them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four towns and the separate travel-time notice.
verses.before: The children of Israel journeyed and came to their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim.
verses.after: The Israelites set out and reached their towns on the third day: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel journeyed and came to their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim.

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath’s divine witness and the tension between restraint and collective protest.
verses.before: But the children of Israel did not strike them because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. Then all the congregation murmured against the leaders.
verses.after: They did not attack them, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole assembly grumbled against the leaders.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the children of Israel did not strike them because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. Then all the congregation murmured against the leaders.

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily touch idiom within their explanation of sworn restraint.
verses.before: But all the leaders said to the whole congregation, “We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
verses.after: All the leaders told the assembly, “We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. We cannot touch them now.
verses.tsw_comparator: But all the leaders said to the whole congregation, “We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.

verses.rationale: Makes their proposed course clear and retains the threatened wrath without adding an explicit subject.
verses.before: This we will do to them: we will let them live, so that wrath may not come upon us because of the oath that we swore to them.”
verses.after: This is what we must do: let them live, so that wrath does not fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This we will do to them: we will let them live, so that wrath may not come upon us because of the oath that we swore to them.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the quoted decision from the narrated labor outcome and preserves the repeated leaders’ role.
verses.before: The leaders said concerning them, “Let them live.” So they became woodcutters and water carriers for all the congregation, as the leaders had spoken concerning them.
verses.after: “Let them live,” the leaders said. So they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole assembly, as the leaders had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The leaders said concerning them, “Let them live.” So they became woodcutters and water carriers for all the congregation, as the leaders had spoken concerning them.

verses.rationale: Names the summoned group and keeps the charge in Joshua’s own question.
verses.before: Joshua called for them and spoke to them, saying, “Why did you deceive us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you live among us?
verses.after: Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and asked, “Why did you deceive us by saying, ‘We live very far from you,’ when you actually live among us?
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua called for them and spoke to them, saying, “Why did you deceive us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you live among us?

verses.rationale: Retains the lasting enslavement and cultic labor rather than calling it voluntary service.
verses.before: Now therefore you are cursed. There will never cease to be servants from among you, woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”
verses.after: Now you are cursed. Some of you will always be slaves, cutting wood and carrying water for the house of my God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore you are cursed. There shall never cease to be servants from among you, woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps their fear of annihilation as their stated reason, without moralizing the deception.
verses.before: They answered Joshua and said, “Because it was certainly told to your servants that the LORD your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. So we feared greatly for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.
verses.after: They answered Joshua, “Your servants were told plainly that the LORD your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and destroy all its inhabitants before you. We feared greatly for our lives because of you, so we did this.
verses.tsw_comparator: They answered Joshua and said, “Because it was certainly told to your servants that the LORD your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. So we feared greatly for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hand image of vulnerability and their appeal to Joshua’s judgment.
verses.before: Now look, we are in your hand. Do to us as is good and right in your eyes.”
verses.after: Now we are in your hand. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now look, we are in your hand. Do to us as is good and right in your eyes.”

verses.rationale: Makes the resulting rescue and its lethal alternative explicit.
verses.before: So he did to them and delivered them from the hand of the children of Israel, and they did not kill them.
verses.after: Joshua dealt with them in this way: he rescued them from the Israelites, who did not kill them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he did to them and delivered them from the hand of the children of Israel, and they did not kill them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the continuing imposed labor, dual recipients and still-prospective chosen place.
verses.before: On that day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this day, at the place that he would choose.
verses.after: That day he made them woodcutters and water carriers for the assembly and for the LORD’s altar, at the place the LORD would choose. They remain so to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this day, at the place that he would choose.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the long report and keeps both destruction and the Gibeonite alliance as triggers.
verses.before: When Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,
verses.after: Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king as he had treated Jericho and its king. He also heard that Gibeon’s people had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,

verses.rationale: Preserves the plural fear, comparison rather than identity with a royal city, and stated military strength.
verses.before: he was very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai and all its men were warriors.
verses.after: They were deeply afraid. Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: he was very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai and all its men were warriors.

verses.rationale: Retains every named king and city pairing before the appeal.
verses.before: So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
verses.after: Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent this message to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon:
verses.tsw_comparator: So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the alliance as the stated reason for the attack and the appeal for help.
verses.before: “Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.”
verses.after: “Come up and help me attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated five-city list and the armies’ joint siege action.
verses.before: So the five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered together and went up, they and all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and fought against it.
verses.after: The five Amorite kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces and advanced with all their armies. They camped against Gibeon and attacked it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered together and went up, they and all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and fought against it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hand image and urgent triple appeal from those now claiming protection as servants.
verses.before: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hands from your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
verses.after: The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal: “Do not withdraw your hand from your servants! Come up quickly; save us and help us. All the Amorite kings of the hill country have gathered against us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hands from your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive army and the emphasized warrior group.
verses.before: So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty warriors.
verses.after: Joshua marched up from Gilgal with all the fighting men, including all the mighty warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty warriors.

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed assurance and hand/stand images linking the commission to the battle.
verses.before: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them will stand before you.”
verses.after: The LORD told Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them. I have given them into your hand; not one of them will stand against you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them shall stand before you.”

verses.rationale: Makes the surprise and overnight march a clear causal sequence.
verses.before: Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.
verses.after: Joshua came upon them suddenly after marching all night from Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Keeps the LORD as the continuing grammatical subject; notes that later verbs may be understood of Israel or Joshua.
verses.before: The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, and Israel struck them with a great slaughter at Gibeon and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-Horon and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
verses.after: The LORD threw them into panic before Israel and dealt them a crushing defeat at Gibeon. He pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, and Israel struck them with a great slaughter at Gibeon and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-Horon and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit divine agency, great stones identified as hail, and the comparison of deaths.
verses.before: As they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-Horon, the LORD threw large stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the children of Israel killed with the sword.
verses.after: As they fled from Israel down the slope of Beth-horon, the LORD hurled great stones from heaven on them all the way to Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: As they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-Horon, the LORD threw large stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the children of Israel killed with the sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps the public address, cosmic imagery and poetic parallel without importing a physical explanation.
verses.before: Then Joshua spoke to the LORD on the day when the LORD gave the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.
verses.after: On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD. In the sight of Israel he said: “Sun, stand still over Gibeon; moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua spoke to the LORD on the day when the LORD gave the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the poem, vengeance, cited book, and approximate duration without scientific harmonization.
verses.before: And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies.” Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of heaven and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
verses.after: The sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a full day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies.” Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of heaven and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unique-day claim and divine listening/fighting as the narrator’s conclusion.
verses.before: There was no day like it before or after it, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.
verses.after: There has been no day like it, before or since, when the LORD listened to a man’s voice in this way. For the LORD fought for Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was no day like it before or after it, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the return notice here even though the account resumes the kings’ fate and repeats it at verse 43.
verses.before: Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
verses.after: Then Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Marks the narrative’s return to the hidden kings without changing the earlier return notice.
verses.before: These five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
verses.after: The five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
verses.tsw_comparator: These five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the discovery report and repeated precise location.
verses.before: It was told to Joshua, saying, “The five kings have been found hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”
verses.after: Joshua was told, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told to Joshua, saying, “The five kings have been found hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the cave-mouth image and the guarding rather than immediate execution.
verses.before: Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and appoint men over it to guard them.
verses.after: He ordered, “Roll great stones across the mouth of the cave and post men there to guard them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and appoint men over it to guard them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rear attack and purpose of preventing escape to towns, with the gift assurance.
verses.before: But you, do not stop. Pursue your enemies and strike their rear. Do not allow them to enter their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand.”
verses.after: But do not stop. Pursue your enemies and strike their rear. Do not let them reach their towns, for the LORD your God has given them into your hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, do not stop. Pursue your enemies and strike their rear. Do not allow them to enter their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both the totalizing defeat and stated survivors, rather than deleting their tension.
verses.before: When Joshua and the children of Israel had finished striking them with a very great slaughter until they were consumed, and the survivors who remained of them had entered the fortified cities,
verses.after: Joshua and the Israelites struck them down in a crushing defeat until they were finished. Yet the survivors who escaped reached the fortified towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joshua and the children of Israel had finished striking them with a very great slaughter until they were consumed, and the survivors who remained of them had entered the fortified cities,

verses.rationale: Preserves the tongue image with a short idiom note and retains the Makkedah camp location.
verses.before: all the people returned to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah in peace. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the children of Israel.
verses.after: All the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah. No one turned a sharp tongue against any Israelite.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the people returned to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah in peace. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal of the cave closure and Joshua’s summons.
verses.before: Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring out these five kings to me from the cave.”
verses.after: Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring out these five kings to me from the cave.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated five kings by city and the removal from hiding.
verses.before: They did so and brought out to him from the cave these five kings: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
verses.after: They did so, bringing out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon from the cave.
verses.tsw_comparator: They did so and brought out to him from the cave these five kings: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

verses.rationale: Preserves public humiliation and command/fulfillment repetition without turning the action into a metaphor only.
verses.before: When they brought out these kings to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, “Come near. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.” So they came near and put their feet on their necks.
verses.after: When the kings were brought to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel. He told the commanders who had gone with him, “Come here and put your feet on these kings’ necks.” They came forward and put their feet on their necks.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they brought out these kings to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, “Come near. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.” So they came near and put their feet on their necks.

verses.rationale: Keeps the commission refrain in its specific military setting.
verses.before: Joshua said to them, “Do not fear or be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for thus the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
verses.after: Joshua told them, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and courageous, for this is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to them, “Do not fear or be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for thus the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.”

verses.rationale: Preserves killing before hanging, five trees and the duration of corpse display.
verses.before: Afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees. They hung on the trees until evening.
verses.after: Afterward Joshua struck the kings and killed them, then hung them on five trees. They remained hanging there until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees. They hung on the trees until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps sunset removal, reuse of the hiding cave, and enduring stones.
verses.before: At the time of sunset Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They placed large stones against the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.
verses.after: At sunset Joshua ordered them taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave where they had hidden. Great stones were placed across its mouth; they remain there to this very day.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the time of sunset Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They placed large stones against the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.

verses.rationale: Retains all victims, the herem claim, no-survivor formula and Jericho comparison.
verses.before: Joshua captured Makkedah that day and struck it and its king with the edge of the sword. He devoted them and every life in it to destruction; he left no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.after: That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it and its king to the sword. He devoted them and everyone in the city to destruction, leaving no survivor. He treated Makkedah’s king as he had treated Jericho’s king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua captured Makkedah that day and struck it and its king with the edge of the sword. He devoted them and every life in it to destruction; he left no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.

verses.rationale: Keeps the next itinerary step and the accompanying Israel formula.
verses.before: Then Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah and fought against Libnah.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the agents without softening the exhaustive killing and repeated king comparison.
verses.before: The LORD also gave it and its king into the hand of Israel. He struck it and every life in it with the edge of the sword. He left no survivor in it and did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.after: The LORD gave Libnah and its king into Israel’s hand too. Joshua put the city and everyone in it to the sword, leaving no survivor. He treated its king as he had treated Jericho’s king.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD also gave it and its king into the hand of Israel. He struck it and every life in it with the edge of the sword. He left no survivor in it and did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three-stage advance, camp and attack.
verses.before: Then Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish. He camped against it and fought against it.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish, camped against it, and attacked it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish. He camped against it and fought against it.

verses.rationale: Retains the second-day detail, every-person scope and prior-city comparison.
verses.before: The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it and every life in it with the edge of the sword, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
verses.after: The LORD gave Lachish into Israel’s hand. Joshua captured it on the second day and put it and everyone in it to the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it and every life in it with the edge of the sword, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named relief force and total defeat without claiming capture of Gezer here.
verses.before: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he left him no survivor.
verses.after: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish. Joshua struck him and his people down until no survivor was left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he left him no survivor.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated campaign formula and exact next city.
verses.before: Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon. They camped against it and fought against it.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon, camped against it, and attacked it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon. They camped against it and fought against it.

verses.rationale: Keeps both same-day references and the shift from collective capture to Joshua’s destruction.
verses.before: They captured it that day and struck it with the edge of the sword. He devoted every life in it to destruction that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
verses.after: They captured Eglon that day and put it to the sword. That same day Joshua devoted everyone in it to destruction, just as he had done to Lachish.
verses.tsw_comparator: They captured it that day and struck it with the edge of the sword. He devoted every life in it to destruction that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

verses.rationale: Preserves upward movement and the named route.
verses.before: Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron, and they fought against it.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron, and they fought against it.

verses.rationale: Keeps dependent towns, full human scope and repeated destruction, without harmonizing the earlier death of Hebron’s king.
verses.before: They captured it and struck it, its king, all its cities, and every life in it with the edge of the sword. He left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. He devoted it and every life in it to destruction.
verses.after: They captured Hebron and put it to the sword, along with its king, its dependent towns, and everyone in it. Joshua left no survivor, just as he had done to Eglon. He devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: They captured it and struck it, its king, all its cities, and every life in it with the edge of the sword. He left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. He devoted it and every life in it to destruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves the turn and new target rather than a return to camp.
verses.before: Then Joshua turned, and all Israel with him, to Debir and fought against it.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel with him turned toward Debir and fought against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua turned, and all Israel with him, to Debir and fought against it.

verses.rationale: Retains every repeated comparison and distinguishes capture, killing, and herem language.
verses.before: He captured it, its king, and all its cities, and they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted every life in it to destruction. He left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.
verses.after: He captured Debir, its king, and all its dependent towns. They put them to the sword and devoted everyone in the city to destruction, leaving no survivor. He treated Debir and its king as he had treated Hebron, and as he had treated Libnah and its king.
verses.tsw_comparator: He captured it, its king, and all its cities, and they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted every life in it to destruction. He left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four terrain zones and the narrator’s exhaustive destruction and divine-command claim.
verses.before: So Joshua struck all the land: the hill country, the Negev, the foothills, and the slopes, and all their kings. He left no survivor but devoted every breathing thing to destruction, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
verses.after: Joshua struck the whole region—the hill country, the Negev, the lowlands, and the slopes—and all their kings. He left no survivor and devoted everything that breathed to destruction, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua struck all the land: the hill country, the Negev, the foothills, and the slopes, and all their kings. He left no survivor but devoted every breathing thing to destruction, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.

verses.rationale: Retains both geographical spans without identifying this Goshen with Egypt’s region.
verses.before: Joshua struck them from Kadesh-Barnea as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
verses.after: Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and throughout the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua struck them from Kadesh-Barnea as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Renders once as a single campaign while keeping the stated reason for success.
verses.before: Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
verses.after: Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in a single campaign, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact repeated return notice from verse 15.
verses.before: Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
verses.after: Then Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named initiator and three royal recipients as the start of the alliance list.
verses.before: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
verses.after: When Jabin king of Hazor heard what had happened, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,

verses.rationale: Preserves all terrain zones and the south-of-Chinneroth and western-Dor qualifiers.
verses.before: and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the foothills, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
verses.after: and to the northern kings in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowlands, and in the heights of Dor to the west.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the foothills, and in the heights of Dor on the west,

verses.rationale: Makes the geographical groups audible while retaining each people and location.
verses.before: to the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites in the hill country, and Hivites under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
verses.after: He also sent to the Canaanites in the east and west; the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country; and the Hivites below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites in the hill country, and Hivites under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sand image and emphatic numbers rather than replacing them with a numerical estimate.
verses.before: They went out, they and all their armies with them, a people as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
verses.after: They came out with all their armies—a vast force, as countless as the sand on the seashore—with very many horses and chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went out, they and all their armies with them, a people as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.

verses.rationale: Retains the coalition’s meeting place and military purpose.
verses.before: All these kings met together and came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
verses.after: All these kings assembled and camped together beside the waters of Merom to fight Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these kings met together and came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the precise tomorrow promise and bodily harm to horses rather than a vague disabling order.
verses.before: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear them, for tomorrow about this time I will give all of them slain before Israel. You will hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
verses.after: The LORD told Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over, slain before Israel. Hamstring their horses and burn their chariots.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear them, for tomorrow about this time I will give all of them slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the surprise and shared location as the response to the promise.
verses.before: So Joshua and all the people of war with him came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom and fell upon them.
verses.after: Joshua and all the fighting men with him came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and attacked.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua and all the people of war with him came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom and fell upon them.

verses.rationale: Retains all pursuit endpoints, eastward qualifier and the no-survivor claim.
verses.before: The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, Misrephoth-Maim, and the Valley of Mizpeh toward the east. They struck them until no survivor remained to them.
verses.after: The LORD gave them into Israel’s hand. The Israelites struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, Misrephoth-maim, and the Valley of Mizpeh to the east. They struck them down until no survivor remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, Misrephoth-Maim, and the Valley of Mizpeh toward the east. They struck them until no survivor remained to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact command/fulfillment correspondence and real animal harm.
verses.before: Joshua did to them as the LORD had spoken to him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
verses.after: Joshua did as the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua did to them as the LORD had spoken to him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps the return and the head image explaining Hazor’s prominence.
verses.before: Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor formerly was the head of all these kingdoms.
verses.after: At that time Joshua turned back, captured Hazor, and killed its king with the sword. Hazor had formerly been the head of all these kingdoms.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor formerly was the head of all these kingdoms.

verses.rationale: Preserves all-person and all-breathing claims and distinct burning of the city.
verses.before: They struck every life in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction. Nothing breathing remained, and he burned Hazor with fire.
verses.after: They put everyone in Hazor to the sword, devoting them to destruction. Nothing that breathed was left. Joshua burned Hazor.
verses.tsw_comparator: They struck every life in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction. Nothing breathing remained, and he burned Hazor with fire.

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive summary and stated Mosaic command without approval commentary.
verses.before: Joshua captured all the cities of these kings and all their kings and struck them with the edge of the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses servant of the LORD had commanded.
verses.after: Joshua captured all these royal cities and their kings. He put them to the sword and devoted them to destruction, as Moses, the LORD’s servant, had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua captured all the cities of these kings and all their kings and struck them with the edge of the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses servant of the LORD had commanded.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit limit on burning despite the broad destruction claims.
verses.before: Yet Israel did not burn any of the cities standing on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.
verses.after: Yet Israel did not burn the cities standing on their mounds. Hazor alone was burned by Joshua.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Israel did not burn any of the cities standing on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes retained animals and goods from killed people; keeps the exhaustive breathing formula.
verses.before: All the plunder of these cities and the livestock the children of Israel took as plunder for themselves. But every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them; they left none breathing.
verses.after: The Israelites took all the plunder and livestock from these cities for themselves. But they put all the people to the sword until they had destroyed them, leaving no one breathing.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the plunder of these cities and the livestock the children of Israel took as plunder for themselves. But every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them; they left none breathing.

verses.rationale: Retains the full three-person transmission chain and emphatic complete obedience claim.
verses.before: As the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He did not leave undone a word of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.after: What the LORD commanded his servant Moses, Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua carried it out. He left undone nothing the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He did not leave undone a word of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the apparently overlapping geographical categories rather than reducing them to a generic whole country.
verses.before: Thus Joshua took all that land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the foothills, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its foothills,
verses.after: Joshua took this whole region: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowlands, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its lowlands,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Joshua took all that land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the foothills, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its foothills,

verses.rationale: Retains the north/south endpoints and explicit death of captured kings.
verses.before: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them, and put them to death.
verses.after: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, to Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them down, and killed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them, and put them to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves duration without reconciling it into the single-campaign language of chapter 10.
verses.before: Joshua made war with all these kings for many days.
verses.after: Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua made war with all these kings for many days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sole stated peace exception and distinguishes it from conquest.
verses.before: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took all in battle.
verses.after: No city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon. Israel took all the others in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took all in battle.

verses.rationale: Retains direct divine hardening, purpose and absence of mercy without softening them into mere permission.
verses.before: For it was from the LORD to harden their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that he might devote them to destruction, that there might be no favor for them, but that he might destroy them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.after: It was the LORD who hardened their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that they would be devoted to destruction without mercy and destroyed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it was from the LORD to harden their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that he might devote them to destruction, that there might be no favor for them, but that he might destroy them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named people, three towns and two larger regions with the stated destruction.
verses.before: At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them and their cities to destruction.
verses.after: At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, all the hill country of Judah, and all the hill country of Israel. He devoted them and their towns to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them and their cities to destruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit surviving locations alongside the totalizing regional claim.
verses.before: None of the Anakim was left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did some remain.
verses.after: No Anakim remained in the land of the Israelites. They remained only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
verses.tsw_comparator: None of the Anakim was left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did some remain.

verses.rationale: Retains the whole-land summary and rest language without erasing later notices of land still unpossessed.
verses.before: So Joshua took the whole land according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses. Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.
verses.after: Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses. He gave it to Israel as an inheritance, divided among their tribes. Then the land rested from war.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua took the whole land according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses. Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

verses.rationale: Introduces the catalogue with its eastward orientation and both boundaries.
verses.before: These are the kings of the land whom the children of Israel struck and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including all the Arabah toward the east:
verses.after: These are the kings the Israelites defeated east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise, taking possession of their lands from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including the whole eastern Arabah:
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the kings of the land whom the children of Israel struck and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including all the Arabah toward the east:

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult valley-middle phrase without silently inserting an unnamed town; retains half Gilead and the border river.
verses.before: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley and half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the children of Ammon;
verses.after: Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. His rule extended from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the middle of the valley and half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the Ammonite border.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley and half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the children of Ammon;

verses.rationale: Preserves both seas, double southern sea name and route below Pisgah.
verses.before: and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth toward the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, toward the east, by the way to Beth-Jeshimoth, and southward under the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.after: It also covered the eastern Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth, and southward along the east side of the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, toward Beth-jeshimoth and below the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth toward the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, toward the east, by the way to Beth-Jeshimoth, and southward under the slopes of Pisgah.

verses.rationale: Retains Og’s Rephaim identification and two royal centers.
verses.before: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
verses.after: There was also the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remaining Rephaim, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,

verses.rationale: Keeps every territory and the dividing line between the two royal domains.
verses.before: and ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah, all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
verses.after: He ruled Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all Bashan to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and half of Gilead to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
verses.tsw_comparator: and ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah, all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated servant title and all three recipients, including half Manasseh.
verses.before: Moses servant of the LORD and the children of Israel struck them, and Moses servant of the LORD gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.after: Moses, the LORD’s servant, and the Israelites defeated them. Moses, the LORD’s servant, gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses servant of the LORD and the children of Israel struck them, and Moses servant of the LORD gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

verses.rationale: Marks the catalogue’s westward turn and preserves boundaries and tribal allocation.
verses.before: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck beyond the Jordan toward the west, from Baal-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,
verses.after: These are the kings Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land as a possession to Israel’s tribes, each with its allotted share:
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck beyond the Jordan toward the west, from Baal-Gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,

verses.rationale: Retains all six terrain categories and all six peoples before the kings list.
verses.before: in the hill country, the foothills, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev—the land of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites:
verses.after: the hill country, lowlands, Arabah, slopes, wilderness, and Negev—the land of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.tsw_comparator: in the hill country, the foothills, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev—the land of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites:

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated one tally and Ai’s distinguishing location.
verses.before: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
verses.after: The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai beside Bethel, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;

verses.rationale: Preserves both royal entries and their separate counts.
verses.before: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
verses.after: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

verses.rationale: Keeps Jarmuth then Lachish in the source sequence with individual counts.
verses.before: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
verses.after: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

verses.rationale: Retains two distinct cities and the repeated numerical formula.
verses.before: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
verses.after: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

verses.rationale: Preserves Geder as written rather than changing it to a similar place name elsewhere.
verses.before: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
verses.after: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

verses.rationale: Retains Hormah and Arad as separate counted kings.
verses.before: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
verses.after: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired entries and uncompressed tally.
verses.before: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
verses.after: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

verses.rationale: Preserves both kings, including Bethel as its own entry.
verses.before: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
verses.after: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

verses.rationale: Keeps both names and one for each without adding geographical identification.
verses.before: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
verses.after: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

verses.rationale: Preserves the second name as Lasharon while noting that its initial element may be a preposition before Sharon.
verses.before: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
verses.after: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;

verses.rationale: Retains the northern royal centers in their listed order.
verses.before: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
verses.after: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

verses.rationale: Keeps the compound Shimron-meron as a single entry, preserving the thirty-one total.
verses.before: the king of Shimron-Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
verses.after: the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Shimron-Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

verses.rationale: Retains the two names and separate numerical counts.
verses.before: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
verses.after: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

verses.rationale: Keeps the Carmel qualifier attached to Jokneam.
verses.before: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
verses.after: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated Dor and pinned Gilgal, with a note on Goiim meaning nations.
verses.before: the king of Dor in the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
verses.after: the king of Dor in the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Dor in the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;

verses.rationale: Closes the continuous tally with its final entry and stated total.
verses.before: the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings were thirty-one.
verses.after: the king of Tirzah, one. Thirty-one kings in all.
verses.tsw_comparator: the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings were thirty-one.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated age notice and explicit unfinished possession alongside chapter 11’s summary.
verses.before: Joshua was old, advanced in days. The LORD said to him, “You are old, advanced in days, and very much land remains to possess.
verses.after: Joshua was old, advanced in years. The LORD told him, “You are old, advanced in years, and a great deal of land still remains to be possessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua was old, advanced in days. The LORD said to him, “You are old, advanced in days, and very much land remains to possess.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two initial territorial groups and opens the boundary list.
verses.before: This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,
verses.after: This is the land that remains: all the districts of the Philistines and all the Geshurite territory,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

verses.rationale: Retains the counted-as qualification, five rulers and five places, with Avvim continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: from the Shihor that is east of Egypt northward to the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite; the five rulers of the Philistines—the Gazite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite—and the Avvim
verses.after: from the Shihor east of Egypt to the border of Ekron in the north, counted as Canaanite land; the territory of the five Philistine rulers in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron; and the Avvim
verses.tsw_comparator: from the Shihor that is east of Egypt northward to the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite; the five rulers of the Philistines—the Gazite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite—and the Avvim

verses.rationale: Attaches the opening southward phrase to Avvim while noting an alternative attachment; preserves Mearah as a name.
verses.before: in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
verses.after: in the south; all the Canaanite land, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, as far as the Amorite border;
verses.tsw_comparator: in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;

verses.rationale: Keeps Gebal distinct from Gibeon and all Lebanese endpoints.
verses.before: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Baal-Gad below Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-Hamath;
verses.after: the land of the Gebalites; and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Baal-Gad below Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-Hamath;

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic divine future dispossession and the immediate allocation command as distinct actions.
verses.before: all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-Maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
verses.after: I myself will drive out before the Israelites all the people of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. Only assign the land to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-Maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.

verses.rationale: Keeps nine-and-a-half recipients and the conclusion of divine speech.
verses.before: Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
verses.after: Now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”

verses.rationale: Unfolds with him by the eastern half-tribe identified later in the chapter; notes that the Hebrew pronoun is compressed.
verses.before: With the other half-tribe, the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance that Moses gave them beyond the Jordan toward the east, as Moses servant of the LORD gave them:
verses.after: With the other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and Gadites had received their inheritance east of the Jordan, the land Moses, the LORD’s servant, had given them.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the other half-tribe, the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance that Moses gave them beyond the Jordan toward the east, as Moses servant of the LORD gave them:

verses.rationale: Retains the explicitly named town-in-valley feature and plateau endpoints.
verses.before: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland from Medeba as far as Dibon;
verses.after: It extended from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau from Medeba to Dibon,
verses.tsw_comparator: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland from Medeba as far as Dibon;

verses.rationale: Keeps Sihon’s title, capital and outer boundary.
verses.before: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the children of Ammon;
verses.after: and all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had ruled in Heshbon, as far as the Ammonite border.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the children of Ammon;

verses.rationale: Preserves every territorial claim and leads into the explanation of Og’s kingdom.
verses.before: and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
verses.after: It included Gilead, the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah—
verses.tsw_comparator: and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;

verses.rationale: Retains Og’s two centers, Rephaim identity and the retrospective Mosaic conquest.
verses.before: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He remained from the remnant of the Rephaim. Moses struck them and dispossessed them.
verses.after: the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who had ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the remaining Rephaim. Moses had defeated them and driven them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He remained from the remnant of the Rephaim. Moses struck them and dispossessed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit failure and continued residence rather than reconciling them with the preceding territory claim.
verses.before: But the children of Israel did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.
verses.after: But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites and Maacathites. Geshur and Maacath still live among Israel to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the children of Israel did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live in the midst of Israel to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the offering-specific description of Levi’s inheritance, distinct from the LORD himself in verse 33.
verses.before: Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire of the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he spoke to them.
verses.after: To the tribe of Levi alone he gave no inheritance. The offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he had promised them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire of the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he spoke to them.

verses.rationale: Makes the allocation and its clan basis explicit in the brief introduction.
verses.before: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their clans.
verses.after: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated Aroer and valley-town boundary for Reuben’s specific allotment.
verses.before: Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland by Medeba;
verses.after: Their territory extended from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the town in the middle of the valley and the whole plateau around Medeba.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland by Medeba;

verses.rationale: Introduces the town list with Heshbon’s plateau dependency clearly attached.
verses.before: Heshbon and all its cities that are in the tableland: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon,
verses.after: It included Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
verses.tsw_comparator: Heshbon and all its cities that are in the tableland: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon,

verses.rationale: Retains the three towns in source order as part of the continuing list.
verses.before: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
verses.after: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
verses.tsw_comparator: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

verses.rationale: Keeps the unusual hill-in-valley locator attached to Zereth-shahar.
verses.before: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill of the valley,
verses.after: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
verses.tsw_comparator: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill of the valley,

verses.rationale: Preserves the mixed town and terrain entries rather than converting all into town names.
verses.before: Beth-Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth;
verses.after: Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth—
verses.tsw_comparator: Beth-Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth;

verses.rationale: Keeps both comprehensive territorial claims, all five leaders and their stated association with Sihon.
verses.before: all the cities of the tableland and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck with the leaders of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
verses.after: all the towns of the plateau and the entire kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had ruled in Heshbon. Moses defeated him and the Midianite leaders Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, Sihon’s princes who lived in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the cities of the tableland and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck with the leaders of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the occupation label and explicit death rather than replacing diviner with prophet.
verses.before: The children of Israel also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword among the rest of their slain.
verses.after: Among those they killed with the sword, the Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword among the rest of their slain.

verses.rationale: Renders Jordan and boundary as a boundary formula with the Hebrew wording noted; retains settlements and clan allocation.
verses.before: The border of the children of Reuben was the Jordan and its border. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
verses.after: The Jordan formed Reuben’s boundary. This was the Reubenites’ inheritance, clan by clan, with its towns and villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border of the children of Reuben was the Jordan and its border. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated tribe/descendants description and clan basis.
verses.before: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad according to their clans.
verses.after: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Retains the half-land claim and identifies this Aroer by its Rabbah relation.
