verses.before: Their territory was Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;
verses.after: Their territory included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, opposite Rabbah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their territory was Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;

verses.rationale: Keeps both boundary spans and the difficult Lidbir name without harmonizing it with Debir.
verses.before: and from Heshbon to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;
verses.after: It stretched from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Lidbir.
verses.tsw_comparator: and from Heshbon to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

verses.rationale: Preserves four valley towns, remaining Sihon territory and the eastern river boundary reaching the sea.
verses.before: and in the valley, Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its border as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan toward the east.
verses.after: In the valley it included Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. The Jordan formed its boundary as far as the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the Jordan’s eastern side.
verses.tsw_comparator: and in the valley, Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its border as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan toward the east.

verses.rationale: Retains the closing formula and both settlement types.
verses.before: This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
verses.after: This was the Gadites’ inheritance, clan by clan, with its towns and villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

verses.rationale: Keeps the twice-specified half-tribe and clan-based allocation.
verses.before: Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it belonged to the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their clans.
verses.after: Moses also gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it belonged to that half-tribe’s clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it belonged to the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated Bashan, Jair’s settlements and the exact sixty-town figure.
verses.before: Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
verses.after: Their territory began at Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the settlements of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;

verses.rationale: Keeps both half qualifications and the lineage-to-clan relationship.
verses.before: half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the children of Machir according to their clans.
verses.after: Half of Gilead, together with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal towns of Og in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh—to half of Machir’s descendants, clan by clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the children of Machir according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Preserves the allocation location and its relation to Jericho.
verses.before: These are the inheritances that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan east of Jericho.
verses.after: These were the inheritances Moses assigned on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan opposite Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the inheritances that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan east of Jericho.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine inheritance formulation rather than substituting the offerings of verse 14.
verses.before: But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.
verses.after: But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he had promised them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.

verses.rationale: Names all three responsible leadership groups and the western land setting.
verses.before: These are the inheritances that the children of Israel received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the children of Israel distributed to them,
verses.after: These are the inheritances the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, allotted to them by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel’s tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the inheritances that the children of Israel received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the children of Israel distributed to them,

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit lot procedure and nine-and-a-half count.
verses.before: by lot was their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.after: Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: by lot was their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

verses.rationale: Keeps prior eastern allocation distinct from the current one and states Levi’s exception.
verses.before: For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.
verses.after: Moses had already given the two and a half tribes their inheritance on the other side of the Jordan. He gave the Levites no inheritance among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

verses.rationale: Explains the source’s tribal counting without inventing an extra tribe and retains the Levitical towns exception.
verses.before: For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to live in, with their pasturelands for their livestock and possessions.
verses.after: Joseph’s descendants formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received no share of the land except towns to live in and pasturelands for their livestock and possessions.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to live in, with their pasturelands for their livestock and possessions.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise command/fulfillment statement before Caleb’s request.
verses.before: As the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did, and they divided the land.
verses.after: The Israelites divided the land just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did, and they divided the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves Caleb’s ethnic descriptor, Moses’ distinct title and the shared earlier promise.
verses.before: Then the children of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know the word that the LORD spoke to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-Barnea.
verses.after: The people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, about you and me at Kadesh-barnea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the children of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know the word that the LORD spoke to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-Barnea.

verses.rationale: Retains forty, source location and the heart image rather than replacing it solely with sincerity.
verses.before: I was forty years old when Moses servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back word to him as it was in my heart.
verses.after: I was forty years old when Moses, the LORD’s servant, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land. I brought him back a report from my heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was forty years old when Moses servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back word to him as it was in my heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heart-melting image and Caleb’s contrasting wholehearted following.
verses.before: But my brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, yet I fully followed the LORD my God.
verses.after: My fellow Israelites who went up with me made the people’s hearts melt, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
verses.tsw_comparator: But my brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, yet I fully followed the LORD my God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the oath’s certainty, foot image, descendants, forever and my God inside Moses’ speech.
verses.before: Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘Surely the land on which your foot has trodden will be an inheritance for you and for your children forever, because you fully followed the LORD my God.’
verses.after: That day Moses swore, ‘The land your foot has walked on will surely be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘Surely the land on which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and for your children forever, because you fully followed the LORD my God.’

verses.rationale: Keeps both elapsed forty-five and age eighty-five and the time setting of the promise.
verses.before: And now, look, the LORD has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years from the time the LORD spoke this word to Moses while Israel walked in the wilderness. And now, look, I am eighty-five years old today.
verses.after: Now look—the LORD has kept me alive as he promised. Forty-five years have passed since he spoke these words to Moses, while Israel was traveling in the wilderness. Here I am today, eighty-five years old!
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, look, the LORD has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years from the time the LORD spoke this word to Moses while Israel walked in the wilderness. And now, look, I am eighty-five years old today.

verses.rationale: Preserves Caleb’s claim and the going-out/coming-in idiom rather than importing a modern fitness claim.
verses.before: I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me. As my strength was then, so my strength is now, for war and for going out and coming in.
verses.after: I am still as strong today as I was when Moses sent me. My strength is the same now as then, for battle and for going out and coming in.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me. As my strength was then, so my strength is now, for war and for going out and coming in.

verses.rationale: Retains perhaps, fortified towns and hoped-for dispossession without changing the uncertainty into certainty.

verses.rationale: Renders Arba as a personal name following the source’s man explanation; retains the repeated land-rest formula without adding genealogy here.

verses.after: Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, the great man among the Anakim. Then the land rested from war.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-Arba. Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

verses.rationale: Keeps the alternate name attached to one town so the two-town count remains transparent.
verses.before: Kiriath-Baal—that is, Kiriath-Jearim—and Rabbah: two cities with their villages.
verses.after: Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, and Rabbah—two towns, with their villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: Kiriath-Baal—that is, Kiriath-Jearim—and Rabbah: two cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Marks the wilderness region and retains the first three entries.
verses.before: In the wilderness: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
verses.after: In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,
verses.tsw_comparator: In the wilderness: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah,

verses.rationale: Renders City of Salt transparently and retains the final group’s count.
verses.before: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-Gedi: six cities with their villages.
verses.after: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi—six towns, with their villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-Gedi: six cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Preserves inability and enduring co-residence, keeping allotment distinct from actual possession.
verses.before: But the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive out. So the Jebusites live with the children of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.after: But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. The Jebusites still live with the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive out. So the Jebusites live with the children of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

verses.rationale: Keep the starting point and ascent distinct; the boundary description must not become an invented travel route.
verses.before: The lot for the children of Joseph went out from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, into the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
verses.after: The allotment for Joseph’s descendants ran from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, through the wilderness that rises from Jericho into the hill country at Bethel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot for the children of Joseph went out from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, into the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.

verses.rationale: Retain Bethel and Luz as successive names in this boundary rather than silently harmonizing them as a single location.
verses.before: It went out from Bethel to Luz and crossed to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.
verses.after: From Bethel it went to Luz, then passed into the territory of the Archites at Ataroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It went out from Bethel to Luz and crossed to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.

verses.rationale: Preserve westward descent, the people named, and Lower Beth-horon rather than the upper town.
verses.before: Then it went down westward to the border of the Japhletites as far as the border of Lower Beth-Horon, then to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
verses.after: It descended west to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as Lower Beth-horon and Gezer, and ended at the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then it went down westward to the border of the Japhletites as far as the border of Lower Beth-Horon, then to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.

verses.rationale: Keep both sons under Joseph and the inheritance vocabulary linking the allotments.
verses.before: So the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
verses.after: So Joseph’s descendants, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retain the eastern designation and Upper Beth-horon even where the geographical syntax is compressed.
verses.before: The territory of the children of Ephraim according to their clans was this: the border of their inheritance toward the east was Ataroth-Addar as far as Upper Beth-Horon.
verses.after: This was the territory of Ephraim’s descendants by their clans. The boundary of their inheritance on the east ran from Ataroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The territory of the children of Ephraim according to their clans was this: the border of their inheritance toward the east was Ataroth-Addar as far as Upper Beth-Horon.

verses.rationale: Unfold directional clauses cautiously without supplying an unattested junction or resolving the difficult Michmethath syntax by a new map.
verses.before: The border went out toward the sea. Michmethath was on the north. The border turned eastward to Taanath-Shiloh and passed beyond it eastward to Janoah.
verses.after: The boundary went toward the sea, with Michmethath on the north. It turned east to Taanath-shiloh and passed beyond it on the east to Janoah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border went out toward the sea. Michmethath was on the north. The border turned eastward to Taanath-Shiloh and passed beyond it eastward to Janoah.

verses.rationale: Keep Ataroth distinct from the fuller name in verse 5 and preserve each boundary point in order.
verses.before: It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and went out at the Jordan.
verses.after: From Janoah it descended to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and went out at the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Carry the sentence into the additional towns in verse 9 while retaining the wadi and seaward endpoint.
verses.before: From Tappuah the border went westward to the Wadi Kanah and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their clans,
verses.after: From Tappuah the boundary went west to the Wadi Kanah and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim’s descendants by their clans,
verses.tsw_comparator: From Tappuah the border went westward to the Wadi Kanah and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their clans,

verses.rationale: Make Ephraim’s enclaves within Manasseh understandable without removing towns or their dependent villages.
verses.before: together with the cities set apart for the children of Ephraim within the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.
verses.after: including the towns set apart for Ephraim’s descendants within the inheritance of Manasseh’s descendants—all those towns and their villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: together with the cities set apart for the children of Ephraim within the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.

verses.rationale: Preserve both continued Canaanite residence and coerced labor; the narrator’s to this day is not a modern claim.
verses.before: But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. So the Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day and became forced labor.
verses.after: But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day, subjected to forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. So the Canaanites have lived in the midst of Ephraim to this day and became forced labor.

verses.rationale: Distinguish Joseph’s firstborn from Manasseh’s firstborn and link the eastern grant to Machir’s military characterization.
verses.before: The lot was for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph’s firstborn. Machir, firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan because he was a man of war.
verses.after: An allotment also went to the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph’s firstborn. Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn and the father of Gilead, had received Gilead and Bashan because he was a warrior.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot was for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph’s firstborn. Machir, firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan because he was a man of war.

verses.rationale: Keep all six clan names and the explicit male designation that sets up the daughters’ claim.
verses.before: The lot was also for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their clans: for the children of Abiezer, the children of Helek, the children of Asriel, the children of Shechem, the children of Hepher, and the children of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph according to their clans.
verses.after: The rest of Manasseh’s descendants received allotments by their clans: the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lot was also for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their clans: for the children of Abiezer, the children of Helek, the children of Asriel, the children of Shechem, the children of Hepher, and the children of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph according to their clans.

verses.rationale: Retain every generation and all five women’s names in the source order.
verses.before: Yet Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.after: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

verses.rationale: Use relatives for the women’s broader brothers claim but retain father’s brothers specifically; name Joshua as the implied grantor in context.
verses.before: They came near before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, saying, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” So according to the command of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers.
verses.after: They approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders. “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our relatives,” they said. So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers, as the LORD had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came near before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, saying, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” So according to the command of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers.

verses.rationale: Preserve ten portions and distinguish these from the eastern holdings; continue the explanation into verse 6.
verses.before: Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan that is beyond the Jordan,
verses.after: Ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan that is beyond the Jordan,

verses.rationale: Keep daughters and sons visible as the narrator’s explanation, rather than flattening the women’s inheritance into generic clan allocation.
verses.before: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the children of Manasseh.
verses.after: because Manasseh’s daughters received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh’s descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the children of Manasseh.

verses.rationale: Render rightward as south in this geographical description while retaining the reference to En-tappuah’s inhabitants.
verses.before: The border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which is east of Shechem. The border went southward to the inhabitants of En-Tappuah.
verses.after: Manasseh’s boundary ran from Asher to Michmethath, opposite Shechem. From there it turned south toward the people of En-tappuah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which is east of Shechem. The border went southward to the inhabitants of En-Tappuah.

verses.rationale: Clarify the distinction between surrounding land and town that is essential to the shared boundary.
verses.before: The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.
verses.after: The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on Manasseh’s boundary, belonged to Ephraim’s descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Unfold the compressed enclave description without merging Ephraim’s southern towns with Manasseh’s northern boundary.
verses.before: The border went down to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi, cities belonging to Ephraim were among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh was north of the wadi, and it ended at the sea.
verses.after: The boundary descended to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi were towns belonging to Ephraim among Manasseh’s towns. Manasseh’s boundary was on the north side of the wadi and ended at the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: The border went down to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi, cities belonging to Ephraim were among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh was north of the wadi, and it ended at the sea.

verses.rationale: Keep the two allotments and the collective northern and eastern neighbors rather than assigning both tribes a new boundary.
verses.before: Southward belonged to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. They reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
verses.after: The land to the south belonged to Ephraim, and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as their boundary. They reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: Southward belonged to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. They reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

verses.rationale: Retain the shift from towns to inhabitants and the difficult three-heights phrase; explain its uncertain relation to the six named places in a note.
verses.before: In Issachar and Asher Manasseh had Beth-Shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of En-Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of Taanach and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages—the three heights.
verses.after: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh had Beth-shean and its dependent towns, Ibleam and its dependent towns, and the inhabitants of Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo, each with its dependent towns—the three heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: In Issachar and Asher Manasseh had Beth-Shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of En-Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of Taanach and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages—the three heights.

verses.rationale: Keep inability distinct from later failure to expel and preserve the Canaanites’ determination.
verses.before: Yet the children of Manasseh were not able to possess these cities, and the Canaanites persisted in living in that land.
verses.after: Yet Manasseh’s descendants could not take possession of these towns. The Canaanites were determined to remain in that land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the children of Manasseh were not able to possess these cities, and the Canaanites persisted in living in that land.

verses.rationale: Preserve coercion and the emphatic failure to expel rather than presenting forced labor as complete conquest.
verses.before: When the children of Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
verses.after: When the Israelites grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but they still did not drive them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the children of Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.

verses.rationale: Retain the paired allotment and portion complaint and its appeal to continuing blessing.
verses.before: The children of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, “Why have you given me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance, since I am a numerous people, because the LORD has blessed me until now?”
verses.after: Joseph’s descendants said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one allotment, one portion, as an inheritance? We are a numerous people, since the LORD has blessed us all this time.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, “Why have you given me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance, since I am a numerous people, because the LORD has blessed me until now?”

verses.rationale: Preserve the conditional challenge, forest clearing, and both named peoples rather than turning the reply into an unconditional new grant.
verses.before: Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up for yourself to the forest and clear land for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”
verses.after: Joshua replied, “If you are so numerous, go up into the forest and clear land for yourselves there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up for yourself to the forest and clear land for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”

verses.rationale: Keep the two areas and the chariots of iron as the speakers’ stated obstacle without supplying a metallurgical explanation.
verses.before: The children of Joseph said, “The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley land have iron chariots, both those in Beth-Shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel.”
verses.after: Joseph’s descendants answered, “The hill country is not enough for us. And all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both those in Beth-shean and its dependent towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Joseph said, “The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley land have iron chariots, both those in Beth-Shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel.”

verses.rationale: Name both groups addressed and preserve the paired people and strength assurance before the practical challenge.
verses.before: Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, saying, “You are a numerous people and have great strength. You will not have only one lot.
verses.after: Joshua said to Joseph’s household, to Ephraim and Manasseh, “You are a numerous people, and you have great strength. You will have more than one allotment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, saying, “You are a numerous people and have great strength. You shall not have only one lot.

verses.rationale: Keep forest clearing and expulsion as distinct actions and preserve the concessive force despite the enemy’s equipment and strength.
verses.before: But the hill country will be yours. Though it is a forest, you will clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours. For you will drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they are strong.”
verses.after: The hill country will be yours. Though it is forest, you must clear it, and its farthest reaches will be yours. You will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the hill country shall be yours. Though it is a forest, you shall clear it, and its farthest limits shall be yours. For you shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they are strong.”
